title: Gullak Season 5 Is Here. The Mishras Have Wi-Fi Now. They're Still Fighting About Money.
excerpt: India's most beloved middle-class family returns on SonyLIV for an unprecedented fifth season — and the reviews say it still feels like coming home, even if the paint won't dry.
body:
Every Indian streaming platform is competing to out-dark each other. Gangsters, serial killers, corrupt politicians, courtroom conspiracies — the grimmer, the better. And then there is *Gullak*, which opens its fifth season with the Mishra family getting their house painted.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=yhxf4SYE1gg</youtube>

The paint takes too long to dry. That's the drama. That's the conflict. And somehow, across seven episodes now streaming on **SonyLIV**, it is more than enough.

Created by **TVF**, *Gullak* is officially the first Indian web series to reach five seasons — a quiet record for a show that has never relied on cliffhangers, shock value, or a single gunshot. What it has relied on, consistently and stubbornly, is the idea that a lower-middle-class family in a small Indian town can be endlessly interesting. Five seasons in, the bet is still paying off.

## What's New in Mishra Niwas

The biggest visible change: the Mishras now have a Wi-Fi router. The gullak — the ceramic piggy bank that gave the show its name — has been relocated to accommodate it. If that sentence makes you feel something, this show was made for you.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DZMrrrzMzLY/

**Jameel Khan** returns as Santosh Mishra, the patriarch whose pride and anxieties run on parallel tracks. He's now chasing the dream of a new house, wading through the bureaucratic swamp of government housing loans. **Geetanjali Kulkarni** is back as Shanti, this time grappling with questions about her identity beyond wife and mother — and dealing with her brother Pinky (**Gopal Datt**), who arrives with an offer concerning her old maternal home.

The sons are evolving too. Annu, now played by **Anant V. Joshi** (replacing Vaibhav Raj Gupta in a notable recast), has moved into a rented flat with friends, chasing a degree of independence from the household's gravitational pull. Meanwhile, younger son Aman (**Harsh Mayar**) has discovered a deeply questionable side hustle as an online astrologer — dispensing cosmic advice and predictably landing himself in trouble.

And then there's Bittu Ki Mummy (**Sunita Rajwar**), who has reinvented herself as a social-media feminist and *mahila mandal* president. If that sounds chaotic, you've clearly never lived next door to someone who discovered Instagram activism at forty.

## What the Critics Are Saying

**Filmfare** gave it 3.5 out of 5, calling it *"one of the most authentic and emotionally resonant shows produced in India"* and praising its ability to *"find meaning in the ordinary."* The review highlights Shanti's arc — her refusal to let her future daughter-in-law make sacrifices in the name of being an *"acchhi lady"* — as one of the season's most affecting moments.

**India Forums** was slightly more measured at 3 out of 5, noting the paradox at the heart of Season 5: *"That familiarity remains one of the show's biggest strengths. Ironically, it is also becoming one of its biggest challenges."* After five seasons, the Mishras feel like family — but family you've visited so often that the surprises are getting smaller.

**The Hollywood Reporter India** was the outlier, calling it the show's *"greediest season yet"* and arguing that the sameness has become a *"deal-breaker."* Harsh, perhaps, but it names something real: the line between comforting and repetitive is thin, and *Gullak* is walking it.

The consensus? If you loved the first four seasons, you'll feel at home. If you've been waiting for the show to push further, you might wish it took more risks. Either way, it remains one of the only shows on Indian OTT that doesn't need someone to die in episode one to hold your attention.

## Why It Matters for Diaspora Viewers

For NRI audiences, *Gullak* has always been something more than a show. It's a portal. The cadences of small-town Hindi conversation, the specific texture of middle-class family arguments, the way someone pours chai while delivering a devastating emotional truth — these are the details that streaming algorithms can't recommend and Hollywood can't replicate.

Season 5 continues in that tradition, tackling themes that hit differently when you're watching from thousands of miles away: the cost of independence, the weight of family expectations, the guilt of leaving, the comfort of return. When Santosh Mishra agonizes over accepting money from his son for a house renovation, he's not just a fictional father. He's every father who would rather live with peeling walls than admit he needs help.

**SonyLIV** is accessible in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia. All seven episodes of *Gullak* Season 5 are streaming now. If you haven't caught up on previous seasons, they're all on the same platform — and frankly, you should.

*Gullak Season 5 is streaming now on SonyLIV. Seven episodes. No murders, no conspiracies, no CGI. Just family.*
